cards.text: Back in 1 Chronicles 17:10, God made David a promise: "And I will subdue all your enemies." Now it's some time later, and David heads out to war. Friend, tie that apron tight, because this chapter moves FAST.

cards.question: Some time after God's promise, David goes to war against an old enemy of Israel. Which people does David defeat and subdue?

cards.text: David even takes Gath and its villages right out of the Philistines' hand. Gath is Goliath's hometown (1 Samuel 17:4), so the shepherd with the sling who beat Goliath (1 Samuel 17:50) just took over the man's whole ZIP CODE.

cards.question: David also defeats the Moabites. What happens to Moab after that?

answers.text: They serve David and bring tribute
They flee and leave their land
They join David as equal partners

cards.text: Then the big one: Hadadezer, king of Zobah, marching out to establish his dominion along the Euphrates River. David defeats him as far as Hamath.

cards.question: David captures a thousand of King Hadadezer's chariots, plus thousands of his soldiers. What does David do with the horses?

answers.text: Sends back all but a hundred

cards.text: Then the Arameans of Damascus come to help Hadadezer, and David strikes down twenty-two thousand of their men. That's like running in to back up your friend in an argument, and now YOU'RE losing the argument too.

cards.question: David places garrisons in Aram of Damascus. True or false: the Arameans become subject to David and bring him tribute.
After all these wins, the chapter tells us who is behind them: So the ___ made David victorious wherever he went.

cards.text: David takes the gold shields that belonged to Hadadezer's officers and brings them to Jerusalem. That's like winning the company softball game and walking out with the OTHER team's trophies too.

cards.question: From Tibhath and Cun, cities of King Hadadezer, David takes a large amount of bronze. Who later uses that bronze to make the bronze Sea and the pillars?
King Tou of Hamath had been at war with Hadadezer. When Tou hears that David defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sends his son Hadoram to greet King David and ___ him.

cards.text: Hadoram brings all kinds of articles of gold and silver and bronze. Friend, that's not a thank-you card, that's a thank-you WAREHOUSE.

cards.question: King David now has Hadoram's gold, silver and bronze, plus the silver and gold he carried off from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines and the Amalekites. What does David do with all of it?

answers.text: Pays the men in his army

cards.text: And there's more. Abishai, son of David's sister Zeruiah (1 Chronicles 2:16), strikes down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.

cards.question: After the Valley of Salt, garrisons are placed in Edom. True or false: only some of the Edomites become subject to David.
That line again: the LORD made David victorious wherever he went. Now David reigns over all Israel and administers ___ and righteousness for all his people.

cards.text: David's got a whole crew, from Joab son of Zeruiah over the army to Zadok and Ahimelech as priests, with David's sons as chief officials at the king's side. My crew is me, my mustache and one very patient oven.

findings.problem: Solomon appears for the first time only as an unexplained name in the answer choices, and no later card says who he is. Give him a simple identification, such as David's son, as is done for the other new people in the passage.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
